summary: First-byte lag (TTFB) regression observed for interactive chat sessions after runtime 1.3 rollout
description:
Issue summary:
AcmeRetail reports a significant increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for interactive chat completions starting 2026-03-12 08:10 UTC. Spike coincides with staged rollout of runtime 1.3.0 and a model pin update to redwood-2.1-chat for the customer's dedicated pool.

Impact:
- ~25% of chat requests for AcmeRetail are experiencing TTFB > 800ms (baseline ~120-200ms).
- User-facing chat UI shows delayed first message; streaming resumes normally after first token in many cases.
- No increase in 5xx rates observed. Throughput steady but tail latency elevated.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool for AcmeRetail in prod us-east.
- Runtime image: runtime:1.3.0 rolled out via canary starting 2026-03-12 07:00 UTC.
- Model pin: redwood-2.1-chat (quantized variant) applied to customer config at 07:45 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Send /v1/chat/completions request with streaming enabled, 1 prompt, max_tokens=512.
2. Observe initial handshake and TTFB until first token.
3. Compare with same request to older runtime instance (if available).

Observed behavior:
- Median TTFB increased from ~150ms to ~420ms; 95th percentile now ~1.2s.
- Streaming socket remains open; tokens arrive after the initial delay.
- No 429 or 5xx for affected requests.

Expected behavior:
- TTFB should remain within previous baseline (<= 250ms median) for interactive workloads.

Initial hypothesis:
1) Runtime 1.3.0 introduced an additional model warmup or kernel selection step on first token path that increases TTFB under certain batch sizes.
2) Model pin to redwood-2.1-chat caused fallback to a quantized kernel path that triggers an extra KV cache validation on initial request.
3) Autoscaling / pool scheduling is queuing requests differently post-rollout (scheduling overhead).

Immediate customer impact and mitigation request:
- Customer requests a fast rollback to previous runtime image or routing to pre-rollout nodes for critical traffic.

Attachments/logs:
- Excerpts from customer's request traces (attached to ticket).
- Grafana dashboard links: latency-by-route, serving-runtime-kernel-metrics, pool-scheduling-latency.
- Sample request IDs: req_us_east_20260312_081220_ae1, req_us_east_20260312_081456_bf2
investigation_notes:
2026-03-12 09:00 UTC - Support acknowledgement and triage (Priya): customer-facing reply sent, escalated to Infra/Runtime.
2026-03-12 09:22 UTC - Runtime team (Ethan) started correlation: matched rollout windows to TTFB increase; canary nodes show similar but smaller increase.
2026-03-12 09:45 UTC - Observed that kernel-selection calls (kernel_selector.v1) had increased latency on runtime 1.3.0 hosts (~200ms extra) traced to a synchronous checksum verification introduced in PR #4521.
2026-03-12 10:15 UTC - Model router traces show additional KV-cache validation on first request after model pin; this path is executed before streaming handshake completes.
2026-03-12 10:40 UTC - No related 5xx or memory pressure; CPU and GPU utilization normal. Scheduling queues show a small rise in enqueue latency but not enough to explain full delta.
2026-03-12 11:05 UTC - Reproduced locally by invoking redwood-2.1-chat with streaming and tracing enabled against runtime:1.3.0; TTFB matched customer numbers.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:03 - Priya Kaur (Support): Acknowledged issue and requested request IDs + recent traces. Customer provided traces and confirmed issue started after their pool received a runtime update.
2026-03-12 09:30 - Ethan Morales (Runtime): Investigating. Noted overlap with runtime:1.3.0 rollout. Adding runtime and model-router owners. Linking PR 4521 for kernel selection change.
2026-03-12 10:00 - AcmeRetail (Customer): We see chat UI lagging for many users. Business impact: reduced conversions for chat-driven checkout flows. Will need rollback if not fixed quickly.

2026-03-12 10:50 - Ethan Morales (Runtime): Found synchronous checksum/validation step in kernel selection introduced in PR 4521 that can add ~150-250ms on first-token path. Working on a branch to make that async or cached per-model instance.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Support (Priya): Provided temporary mitigation steps to route traffic away from updated nodes. Customer requested a safe rollback; COO approved emergency rollback for dedicated pool if needed.
2026-03-12 12:05 - SRE (Jasmine Liu): Prepared canary rollback plan and vetted rollback playbook. Will coordinate with runtime team and notify customer of timing.
next_steps: 1) Runtime team to push a hotfix that either caches checksum result or makes validation async (target: 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC). 2) If hotfix not available within 4 hours of update, perform controlled rollback of customer dedicated pool to runtime:1.2.x per rollback playbook. 3) After mitigation, run A/B comparison using telemetry and customer-run smoke tests. 4) Post-incident writeup linked to INT-4107.
workaround: Route AcmeRetail traffic to nodes still on runtime:1.2.x (manual routing via pool-tag) or temporarily pin customer to pre-rollout model variant. Support provided detailed steps for ops routing; customer confirmed access to their routing controls.
resolution_notes: (Pending) - Investigation indicates runtime change in PR 4521 is root cause; fix branch created. Action to deploy hotfix or rollback based on mitigation testing. Final resolution will be appended when complete.
notes_for_postmortem: If fix is implemented, include timeline of runtime 1.3 rollout, decision to include synchronous checksum, and testing gap that missed TTFB regression for streaming first-token path. Recommend adding a TTFB smoke test to the runtime CI for streaming endpoints.
